Great idea for a sub! I am leaking some oil on my 2002 Tundra that I just bought and the mechanic wants me to get an engine pressure wash to see where it is. Necessary?

I would think that if your motor is excessively grimy/dirty it would make it more difficult to locate the leak.

  • Necessary: unlikely
  • Very Helpful: most definitely.

Yes, It's very hard to see a leak when the whole surface is splattered in oil. Lots of time the oil leak is in a spot where gravity makes it drip and fall in a moving part (like a pulley or or a hose) and causes the oil to splatter and drip everywhere.

If you wanan save some bucks you can clean it yourself with degreaser and a brush but check with your sates law. In FL for example it is illegal to do this at your hose or most car washes because of the chemical disposal. This is most likely why your mechanic will not do it for you.

An alternative approach is to perform a UV dye test to find the source of the leak(s). To do this a dye is added to the oil and the vehicle is driven for a day or so to allow time for oil to leak out. Then, starting from the bottom a UV light is used to look for fresh oil; the dye will glow bright yellow under UV light, leading upwards to the leak source. This particular test works better on an engine that has not been cleaned first, as existing dirt and oil help to make new leakage stay intact and visible. This method works very well, especially for small leaks that can take several days to show symptoms.

After the leaks are repaired, then you should degrease and clean your engine, so that if there are still any leaks after the repair you will know about them.

It's crummy out and we've been banging around the house all morning. I've got a $40 budget and 10 year old boy/girl twins. Let's hear some ideas!
Bored with the kids on a rainy day. What cheap non-outdoor activities for 10 year old kids do you recommend?
I used to ride mattresses down the stairs, maybe not the safest plan, but I usually had a great time!
Build a pillow fort and watch some movies! Perfect for a rainy day.

make a book safe. Have kids each pick one old book, and grownup does the cutting. Find a HOWTO online.

Then they can play spy / secret agent, etc...
Boardgames, make some food together, smoke weed, watch movies.
Got some xbox or playstation controllers? Hook em up to your computer, download some sweet playstation / SNES / N64 emulators and games and play some multiplayer games. :)

I used to build models with my dad and I really think it was fun as well as an awesome learning experience. Super rewarding. We built models of the space shuttle and did model trains. Trains might not be the cheapest, but you can buy model kits pretty cheap.
Make your own t-shirts. Buy a white pack of shirts and fabric markers
I would sit them down for a good ol' fashioned tabletop rpg. I found some free ones that only require paper and/or dice.
Making homemade slime is always fun! Here's a pretty good guide on how to make it. I recommend adding glitter too!

It sounds like you're also looking to get out of the house, so I would recommend an indoor play place or, if its in your area, a dollar show movie theater. Typically, we wind up doing one of those things with my son when he's starting to pull his hair out. Or, we'll just go and walk around the mall and let him play in the play area there.
Tie pillows around them, or use duct tape, super wrestling party sumo smackdown fun time! If they have the mind for it you could try teaching them some card games.
Build an obstacle course out of blankets, tables, couch cushions, etc. They have to take the time to build it, then you time then running through it.
